lines: Pick a plan, press Start ride, and Wattzup drives the bike for you.
Set up your ride. HIIT intervals are hard and easy efforts on repeat, and the resistance switches at every interval.
Press Tabata: eight rounds of twenty seconds on, and ten off.
The preview adds up the ride before you start.
Start ride sends the plan. Starting, then the dashboard.
Here you are in round five of eight: work at level eighteen, with half a minute to go.
Next: recover for twenty seconds at level six.
When a segment starts, the plan sends its level to the bike.
Sent to bike lists every command, and the bike acknowledges each one.
Every change is called out. Work, eighteen, go!
Power versus plan draws your effort against every target.

lines.text: On a phone, the dashboard is one column.
On a desktop, the resistance sits beside it.

lines: What no screen shows: if the bike drifts off the level, the plan sends it again every five seconds.
And if a send fails, the ride keeps going.
That is journey one. Wattzup turns an Echelon bike or treadmill into a live training display.
